headline: In 2024-2026 a 10% one-day rise in heating-oil futures went with a 2.0% fall in United's market-hedged share return on the same day (95% interval -2.9% to -1.2%, n = 662 sessions). After a 10% five-session rise in heating-oil futures in 2024-2026, United's market-hedged return over the next 20 and 60 sessions is not distinguishable from zero: neither a continued fall nor a rebound (20 sessions: -0.4%, 95% interval -2.9% to +2.5%; 60 sessions: -4.7%, 95% interval -13.1% to +1.6%; n = 636 to 676 overlapping sessions).
plain_summary: In 2024-2026 a 10% one-day rise in heating-oil futures went with a 2.0% fall in United's market-hedged share return on the same day (95% interval -2.9% to -1.2%, n = 662 sessions). The same measure was -1.3% in the fit split (2013-2019) and +0.6% in the select split (2020-2023), not distinguishable from zero.

After a 10% five-session rise in heating-oil futures in 2024-2026, United's market-hedged return over the next 20 and 60 sessions is not distinguishable from zero: neither a continued fall nor a rebound (20 sessions: -0.4%, 95% interval -2.9% to +2.5%; 60 sessions: -4.7%, 95% interval -13.1% to +1.6%; n = 636 to 676 overlapping sessions).

Large fuel rises (five-session heating-oil change above its own past 95th percentile, first of each cluster): 6 events in 2024-2026 with non-overlapping windows, 11 before thinning; United's abnormal return over the next 60 sessions is not distinguishable from zero (+0.2% on average, 95% interval -31.4% to +31.9%).

Trading-rule check (UAL hedged with SPY, long after a large fuel rise and short after a large fuel fall, entered at the next close and held 10 sessions; picked from 144 variants on the select split; 5 basis points per side): test-split annualised Sharpe -0.67 with standard error 0.60 over 16 trades, deflated Sharpe ratio 0.00 (Sharpe -0.78 in the fit split and 1.37 in the select split); nothing survives costs: the Sharpe ratio is not distinguishable from zero.

verdict.label: neither
verdict.rule: under_reaction if the stock keeps falling after a fuel rise, over_reaction if it rises back, neither if the 95% interval spans zero; decided on the lagged regression in the locked split

timing: Grid: one row per US equity session; a series that did not print is missing there and is never filled.
HO=F on session t is treated as known at the equity close of t and is paired with equity returns of sessions t+1 onward in every predictive test.

Yahoo does not document whether its HO=F close is the 14:30 settlement or a later trade, so the primary lagged regression is also computed with one more session skipped and the trading rule is tried with both entries.
The EIA spot print for session t is treated as known one business day later and is paired with equity returns of sessions t+2 onward. It is the current vintage of the series.
Same-session regressions are descriptive co-movement, not tradable.
Beta for session t uses sessions t-252 to t-1 only.
Event thresholds use only sessions before the event; market-model windows end before the event window.
A row or event belongs to a split only if its whole outcome window ends inside that split.
The first session of each month is a contract roll for HO=F; its return is treated as missing.

decisions: Fuel series: HO=F because it trades and is known before the equity close; the EIA spot series is shown beside it with its publication lag.

Contract rolls: on the first session of a month the HO=F return compares two contracts. In fit and select those sessions show a wider gap to the spot series than other sessions, so the return is treated as missing.

Overlap rule: thinning chosen before any outcome was read. The rule in stats.py ("drop_later") removes an event when any earlier event lies within 65 sessions, kept or not; in fit and select fuel events come in chains, so it left no fuel-rise event with a usable window in 2020-2023. The primary rule keeps an event unless a kept event lies within 65 sessions before it: windows of kept events never intersect and no later event is consulted. Both, and the flagged set, are reported.

Abnormal return: the market model without its intercept (return minus beta x SPY, beta from the 250 sessions before the event window). An intercept estimated on 250 sessions and subtracted for 66 carries the share's own pre-event trend into the result; in the select split it changed the 60-session figure for fuel rises materially (the intercept variants in variants_tried show both). The intercept-free figure is also the return of the hedged position that the regressions and the trading rule use. The version with the intercept is reported beside it.
Market-model estimation uses all 250 prior sessions: removing sessions inside earlier event windows left too few events.
Lagged signal: the trailing 5-session HO=F change, the quantity that defines an event; chosen before results were read.
Trading rule: chosen by code as the highest net Sharpe on the select split among variants with at least 10 trades there; the fit split is reported for the chosen rule and takes no part in the choice.
development_log: Pass 1 (data to the end of the select split only): strict thinning, market model with intercept, estimation without event-window sessions, rule variants on thinned events of one side. Too few events survived. Its variants are regenerated in variants_tried under 'first development pass' and as the 'strict' rule family.

Pass 2 (same data): primary thinning rule, estimation on all prior sessions, market model with intercept, rule variants on thinned events. Regenerated under 'second development pass' and as the 'thinned' rule family.

Pass 3 (same data): intercept dropped from the abnormal return; rule variants on every event with one position at a time, as rebound or drift bets on rises, falls or both (the 'all' rule family); fuel move net of the market added as a variant. This is the frozen specification.
No number from the test split was computed or read before the specification was frozen.

caveats: HO=F is NY Harbor diesel, not Gulf Coast jet fuel; it is used because it trades and settles before the equity close.
HO=F is Yahoo's continuous front-month series: roll dates are inferred (first session of each month) and that session's return is dropped; Yahoo does not document whether its close is the settlement.
The EIA spot series is the current vintage; the one-business-day publication lag is an assumption.
